newsitem.title: CANADA: FOCUS-Canada denies PolyGram film distribution rights.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Canada denies PolyGram film distribution rights.

text.p: Canada on Thursday denied an application by PolyGram to distribute foreign films in the country, but granted the Dutch-owned film company the right to set up a Canadian production company.
Canada's Industry Minister John Manley said PolyGram would be allowed to operate a fully integrated Canadian film company involving film, video and television production and distribution.
But PolyGram, which is 75 percent owned by Dutch consumer electronics giant Philips Electronics NV, must continue to distribute its foreign films in Canada through intermediaries.
"They are not going to be doing film distribution. They're going to be doing film production. They've agreed to abide by the law," Manley's spokesman Bill Milliken told Reuters.

"The policy is under review but there was no way it was going to be completed prior to the election, and PolyGram wanted to get on with business, so they said, 'OK, we'll abide by the policy, let's go,'" Milliken said.
A federal election is expected in Canada this year.

Although Ottawa restricts foreign film distribution in Canada as part of its policy of cultural protectionism, some Hollywood distributors have been allowed, under a "grandfathering policy", to distribute American films here.

PolyGram had sought but failed to win the same exemption. "The company will comply with the government film distribution policy and has committeed to reinvest C$20 million ($15 million U.S.) or 20 percent of its Canadian revenues in film products in Canada over a five-year period," the government said in a statement.
The decision appeared to be a victory for Canada's Heritage Minister Sheila Copps, regarded as a "culture hawk" for her strong interest in protecting Canadian culture.
"PolyGram's plan is consistent with Canadian film distribution policy and furthers our objective which is to build a strong and healthy Canadian film industry," Copps said.
The separatist Bloc Quebecois, the official opposition in parliament, had also urged the government to block PolyGram from distributing foreign movies in Canada.
